news.title: UEFA Threatens FIFA Boycott Over Gianni Infantino's World Cup Stake Sale Proposal
news.lede: Switzerland , July 30, 2026 - European football has been plunged into one of its biggest governance disputes in decades after UEFA warned it is prepared to boycott future FIFA competitions if FIFA president Gianni Infantino proceeds with a controversial plan to sell a minority stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup and other major tournaments to private investors. The proposal has sparked fierce opposition from UEFA, several national associations and other football stakeholders, raising concerns over the future governance and ownership of the world's biggest sporting event. What FIFA is Proposing At the center of the controversy is Infantino's proposal to create a new commercial entity called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

news.title: Uefa agrees to boycott Fifa competitions if World Cup sell-off plans proceed
news.lede: Uefa vote passes 55-0 at emergency meeting on Thursday. Boycott would begin with next year’s Women’s World Cup. European countries have agreed to boycott all Fifa competitions if Gianni Infantino pushes forward with his proposals to sell chunks of the World Cup to US-based private investment. In an extraordinary development all 55 Uefa members resolved not to participate in future World Cups or other Fifa-run events, saying in a statement that they “unanimously and unequivocally reject” the proposals.
